comparison: RepoBench-P retrieval strategies, Table 4 (cleanest pair: UniXcoder-L2H / -H2L retrieval vs Random cross-file snippets, both filled to the 6,400-token cap). RepoBench-R (Table 2) compares retrievers on retrieval accuracy only, with no generating model.
model_config: Same model in every arm: Codex (code-davinci-002), temperature 0.2, 64 generated tokens. Same in-file allocation: 1,600 tokens, at most 60 preceding lines.
dataset_metric: RepoBench-P (Python/Java; XF-F, XF-R, IF); Exact Match and Edit Similarity
budget_control: Explicit equal cap that both arms fill: 'Any unused tokens from this allocation are then filled by the cross-file context, up to a total prompt size of 6,400 tokens'. Random snippets are added 'until the token limit is reached'. Each sample has at least 12,000 (Python) / 24,000 (Java) tokens of candidates, so both arms reach the cap. Realized per-arm token counts are not tabulated.
arm_a: UniXcoder-L2H: cross-file snippets ranked by UniXcoder embedding similarity to the last 3 in-file lines (low-to-high order), filled up to 6,400 tokens
arm_b: Random: randomly selected cross-file snippets, filled up to 6,400 tokens
other_changes: None reported. Random was run only once ('should be considered indicative and not conclusive').
delta: Python All EM 37.11 vs 34.15 (+2.96), ES 74.32 vs 72.72. Java All EM 41.83 vs 40.77.
rationale: Only the snippet-selection mechanism differs, and both arms fill the same hard cap: 'snippets are obtained ... while adhering to a 6,400-token limit' vs 'randomly selected ... until the token limit is reached'. The Baseline arm (6,400 tokens of in-file context only) is also cap-matched. RepoBench-C/P across models do not isolate the representation.
graph_class_check: n/a (no graph/AST/CPG representation; only embedding and lexical retrieval)

comparison: RQ1 Table I (vanilla vs +Local Functions vs +Class Instance Attributes ...); also RQ2 Table II (top-k global functions) and RQ4 Table IV (vanilla / A1 / A2 / A3)
model_config: GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k in all ablation arms. Table IV also compares against GPT-4o (a different model).
dataset_metric: Custom 29-repo / 383-function benchmark; local/global reuse precision/recall/F1 and accuracy, human-annotated
budget_control: Not controlled and not reported. Arms add knowledge to the prompt with no token cap. Table II reports only 'Avg. Retrieved Functions' (1.757 at k=1 up to 23.592 at k=15).
arm_a: Prompt + Local Functions + Class Instance Attributes (local-module knowledge)
arm_b: Prompt + Local Functions only (or vanilla prompt with no local knowledge)
other_changes: None beyond the injected knowledge. The FunDes+FunCode retrieval variant adds an extra LLM call (What-If Code Generator).
delta: Local reuse F1 0.673 vs 0.589 (P +7.94%, R +19.70%, F1 +14.26%). Vanilla accuracy 0.721.
rationale: Same model and pipeline; arms differ only by which knowledge is injected, which also adds context, and no budget is held. Example: 'Upon additionally providing knowledge of Class Instance Attributes, the model's ... F1 score improve by ... 14.26%'.
graph_class_check: AST is listed but is not the primary class (hybrid). AST-derived local knowledge is only compared additively. No budget-matched comparison exists.

comparison: Analogy-only (AC) vs rationale-only (RC) vs dual context (DC) at a fixed small truncation size: Appendix A table, DeepSeek-Coder-7B at 256 (and 512) tokens. Table 1 makes the same comparison at 4096 tokens.
model_config: Same code LM per row (DeepSeek-Coder-7B in Appendix A; Table 1 repeats for several LMs). Same RTG ranking/score function within a row; in-file context max 2,048 tokens for all arms.
dataset_metric: CrossCodeEval Python; Code EM/ES, Identifier EM/F1
budget_control: Hard truncation bound L on total cross-file context, equal across arms ('The total length of all the items in Γ_td is bounded by the length bound L'). At 4096 it is effectively not binding: 'the majority of samples remain untruncated, allowing us to approximate it as Unlimited'. At 256/512 the cap binds, but realized tokens per arm are not reported; only number of contexts is (256/UniXcoder: AC 1.05; DC 0.78 AC + 0.36 RC).
arm_a: DC: analogy chunks plus rationale context (import/dependency-derived modules, classes and functions: call_dep_graph-like), ranked by RTG and truncated to L
arm_b: AC: similarity-retrieved analogy chunks only, truncated to L (or RC: rationale context only)
other_changes: None. Same model, RTG scorer and prompt construction.
delta: DeepSeek-Coder-7B, L=256, UniXcoder ranking, Code EM: DC 17.15 vs AC 15.87 vs RC 14.45. At L=4096 (Table 1) DC 27.92 vs AC 19.70 vs RC 21.13, but there the arms are not size-matched.
rationale: At small L the same hard cap binds for every arm and only the context type differs ('merge the two contexts into a prompt with a fixed size'). The headline Table 1 at 4096 is effectively unlimited, so DC there also carries more content. Caveat: realized per-arm tokens are not reported.
graph_class_check: call_dep_graph is listed but is not primary (hybrid). Yes: a cap-matched comparison of the dependency-derived rationale context exists (RC alone vs AC at L=256/512; DC vs AC). At L=256, RC alone scores below AC (14.45 vs 15.87 EM).

comparison: Table 4 ablation: LingmaAgent vs 'w.o. call_graph' (also w/o summary, w/o mcts & summary, w. review)
model_config: GPT-4-Turbo (gpt-4-1106-preview) in all arms; same agent framework apart from the removed module
budget_control: Not controlled and not reported per arm. Only a fixed MCTS compute budget (600 iterations / 300 s) and an average cost of $3.99 for the full system.
arm_a: Full LingmaAgent: repository knowledge graph with structure tree plus call-graph reference extension during MCTS exploration, plus summary agent
arm_b: w.o. call_graph: 'Only the structure tree in MCTS is retained for tree search, and the reference extension module (i.e., the call relationship graph) is removed'
other_changes: MCTS exploration trajectory, and therefore the number of LLM calls and the gathered context, can differ between arms (not reported)
rationale: One module is removed with the same model and scaffold, but nothing about context size or calls is held or reported: 'removing these modules all resulted in a drop in the performance'. Baseline comparisons (SWE-agent, AutoCodeRover) are multi-change.
graph_class_check: Primary class is call_dep_graph. No budget-matched comparison of the graph representation exists; the only isolating ablation (w.o. call_graph) has uncontrolled, unreported context and calls.

comparison: Project-level code completion, Appendix Table 10: context composers (Naive, Path distance, Half memory, File length, Imports first, Only declarations+PD) at fixed repository-context sizes of 256 / 1,753 / 12,000 tokens
model_config: CodeLlama-7B for all composers; medium-context set
dataset_metric: LCA project-level code completion, medium-context set (48K-192K characters of .py); perplexity on the completion file
budget_control: Equal explicit cap per column: 'A number in the column name means the maximum number of tokens in the context from the repository snapshot'. Medium-set repositories (48K-192K chars) exceed these caps, so concatenative composers fill them. Realized per-composer tokens are not reported.
arm_a: Path distance composer: files ordered by file-tree proximity to the completion file, truncated to the cap (also Imports first: import-related files first)
arm_b: Naive composer: all repository files concatenated in no specific order, truncated to the same cap
other_changes: None; same model, data and cap. Main-text EM results (Table 9) instead compare file-level vs PD 16K, and the other five LCA tasks vary models and context together.
delta: All files @12,000: perplexity PD 1.607 vs Naive 1.761 vs Imports first 1.732 vs Only declarations+PD 1.710 (file-level only: 1.849)
rationale: Only the composer (ordering/selection) changes, under the same token cap on a pool larger than the cap: 'the perplexity values are different, but the order of composers performance is the same'. Caveat: perplexity, not EM. Realized tokens not reported but bounded by the cap.
graph_class_check: n/a as primary (hybrid). An import-relation composer ('Imports first') and a declarations-only skeleton composer are compared at the same cap; both are worse than Path distance.

comparison: Table 2/3: Baseline (in-file only) vs '+ Retrieval' (CrossCodeEval-style Jaccard snippets) for the same code LLM; '+ Retrieval & Tuning' additionally fine-tunes
model_config: Same model per pair (e.g., Code Llama-7B, StarCoder-7B, DeepSeekCoder). The tuning arm changes weights.
dataset_metric: M2RC-Eval (18 languages); EM and ES (plus CodeBLEU)
budget_control: Not matched. The retrieval arm fills 'until the total length ... reaches the predetermined maximum token limit of 4096'. The baseline gets 'Only the original code file', with no equal fill. Input length (512-4096) is varied separately (Fig. 10) on the tuned model only.
arm_a: + Retrieval: Jaccard-ranked 10-line cross-file chunks prepended to the in-file context, up to 4,096 tokens
other_changes: Baseline vs +Retrieval: none. +Retrieval & Tuning adds fine-tuning on M2RC-Instruct (multi-change).
delta: Code Llama-7B, C: EM 18.6 -> 21.8, ES 47.2 -> 47.2 (Table 2; mixed by language, e.g. HTML EM 20.6 -> 12.6)
rationale: Same model and scaffold; only context differs, but the amount differs (in-file only vs filled to 4,096): 'This concatenation continues until the total length ... reaches the predetermined maximum token limit of 4096'.
graph_class_check: AST is listed but only builds the benchmark (cursor selection and bucket/semantic labels); it is never a context representation. No budget-matched comparison of an AST context exists.

comparison: Table 5: embedding model for RAG (bge-large-en-v1.5 vs jina-embeddings-v2-base-en) at the same chunk size, on samples >10k tokens. Table 4, RAG on/off on the same subset, is a close second.
model_config: Same fine-tuned DeepSeek-Coder-Instruct-6.7B (RTLRepoCoder); 10,240-token inference window; temperature 0.2
dataset_metric: RTLLM-Repo-style Verilog repository completion (samples whose context exceeds 10k tokens); ES and EM
budget_control: Explicit equal fill rule: 'The retrieved chunks are then added to C_retr in descending order of relevance until the input length reaches the predefined length L' (10,240). All evaluated samples exceed L, so both arms fill the window. Realized tokens per arm are not reported.
arm_a: RAG with jina-embeddings-v2-base-en (8k-context embedder), 4,096-token chunks, filled to L
arm_b: RAG with bge-large-en-v1.5 (512-token embedder), 4,096-token chunks, filled to L
other_changes: None beyond the retriever embedding model
delta: Chunk 4096: ES 82.8 vs 80.9, EM 53.1 vs 51.0. (Table 4: RAG vs no RAG, ES 83.5 vs 81.2, EM 55.0 vs 50.3.)
rationale: Only the context-selection mechanism changes, and both arms fill the same 10,240-token window on >10k samples ('until the input length reaches the predefined length L'). Caveat: realized lengths are not tabulated, and Table 4's no-RAG truncation rule is not stated.

comparison: Table 2 ablation (w/o Multiple Chain Generation, w/o Multi-Agent Debate, w/o Edit plan). Also Table 3 localization vs SWE-Agent with the same DeepSeek-V3-0324.
model_config: DeepSeek-V3-0324 throughout. The method extends the SWE-Search MCTS framework.
budget_control: Not reported or controlled. No per-arm token counts. Graph traversal breadth/depth is fixed for the full system, but ablated arms change how many chains and agent calls are produced.
arm_a: Full SWE-Debate: K×W fault-propagation chains from dependency-graph traversal, three-round multi-agent debate, edit plan fed to the MCTS editor
arm_b: w/o Multiple Chain Generation: 'the method must rely on single-path exploration'
other_changes: Removing chains or debate changes the number of LLM calls and agents and the downstream pipeline stages. The SWE-Agent comparison changes the entire scaffold.
delta: Pass@1 41.4% vs 31.4% (-10.0 pp); w/o debate 37.2%; w/o edit plan 35.4%. Localization 81.67% vs SWE-Agent 67.00%.
rationale: Each ablation removes a multi-call pipeline stage rather than swapping a representation at fixed context: 'removing the multiple chain generation component causes ... a 10.0 percentage point degradation'. No arm feeds the same model a non-graph context at a matched budget.
graph_class_check: Primary class is call_dep_graph. No budget-matched comparison of the graph representation exists; no token budget is reported for any arm.

comparison: Table 3 ablation: single-path variants CodeRAG_df (dataflow-guided retrieval) vs CodeRAG_s (sparse TF-IDF) vs CodeRAG_d (dense), no reranker
model_config: Same code LLM per column (CodeGen-350M, SantaCoder-1.1B, StarCoder2-3B, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B); temperature 0; max input 2,048; 48 generated tokens
budget_control: Nominal cap only: 'The maximum input length of all code LLMs is set to 2,048 by default'. Arm sizes differ by design: sparse/dense return j=15 results each, while dataflow returns only the dependency chain of the last line. Realized prompt lengths are not reported.
arm_a: CodeRAG_df: code retrieved along data-dependency edges of the unfinished file's dataflow graph
arm_b: CodeRAG_s: TF-IDF sparse retrieval of top-j chunks
other_changes: None reported apart from the retrieval path. The full system adds multi-path fusion and an LLM reranker.
delta: StarCoder2-3B Code EM: df 35.13 vs s 33.83 (+1.30); Qwen2.5-Coder-7B: df 41.86 vs s 39.89
rationale: Same LLM and prompt format; only the retrieval path differs, but the amount retrieved differs and is unreported ('we retrieve j results from each path' vs 'retrieve the dependency starting from the last unfinished line'). The 2,048 limit is a nominal ceiling, not an equalized realized budget.
graph_class_check: AST is listed as primary and cpg_dataflow is also present. No budget-matched comparison exists for either; the dataflow-vs-sparse/dense ablation has unequal, unreported context sizes.

comparison: Table 4: No RAG vs GraphCoder (code-context-graph retrieval) vs RLCoder vs RepoCoder, same model, fixed 2,048-token window. Cleanest single-call pair: GraphCoder vs No RAG (or RLCoder vs No RAG).
model_config: Same model per block (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, etc.; API defaults). RepoCoder is iterative (extra generation rounds), so it is not single-change.
dataset_metric: MHRC-Bench-Eval (Chisel, V/SV, VHDL, HLS); EM/ES, preceding-context and full-context settings
budget_control: Explicit equal window: 'All models use a fixed 2,048-token input window ... within the same window budget'. No-RAG trims context to the limit ('If the context length exceed the token limit, the head of the left context and the tail of the right context are trimmed'). GraphCoder can 'flood the context window'. Realized per-arm tokens are not reported.
arm_a: GraphCoder: snippets retrieved via code context graph (control-flow and data-dependence slices), modified for FIM and HDL, within 2,048 tokens
arm_b: No RAG: in-file preceding (or preceding+succeeding) context trimmed to 2,048 tokens
other_changes: GraphCoder was modified by the authors for HDL/FIM. Retriever hyperparameters were 'tuned per method'. No extra LLM calls for GraphCoder or RLCoder; RepoCoder iterates.
delta: GPT-5, preceding context, Chisel EM 11.1 (GraphCoder) vs 15.2 (No RAG), ES 17.3 vs 51.6. RLCoder 17.9 / 55.3.
rationale: Same model and a single generation call, under the same hard 2,048-token window: 'All models use a fixed 2,048-token input window'. Caveat: realized fill per arm is not reported, so this rests on the hard cap rather than measured equality.
graph_class_check: call_dep_graph is listed but is not primary (hybrid). Yes: a fixed-window comparison of a graph-structured retriever (GraphCoder) against No RAG and RLCoder exists, and the graph arm performs worst on HDL.

comparison: Experiment 2B (Tables 8-9): TREEFRAG LOD-1 tree vs Function Summary vs File Summary vs Naive raw code base. Cleanest: TREEFRAG vs Function Summary (same 12 models; Naive excludes Claude models).
model_config: Same 12 frontier models for TREEFRAG and both summary methods, same Asks, same blinded LLM grader (grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning). The Naive arm omits the Claude models.
dataset_metric: 40 issue reports (Asks) on one proprietary code base (RWT); LLM-graded specification score (mean) and per-Ask rank
budget_control: Not controlled; realized sizes reported, and the structured arm is the smallest: TREEFRAG '8k and 12k' tokens vs File Summary '20k to 23k', Function Summary '53k to 61k', Naive '194k to 239k'
arm_a: TREEFRAG: hierarchical tree of node names only (LOD 1) built by LLM-assisted decomposition, plus the Ask
arm_b: Function Summary: per-function LLM summaries of the code base, plus the Ask
other_changes: Both arms rely on offline LLM preprocessing (tree decomposition vs summarisation). Single prompt per arm. Single code base, single author, LLM-as-grader.
delta: Mean score 91.95 vs 92.05 (-0.10); mean rank 20.69 vs 21.34; first place 22/40 vs 11/40
rationale: Same models, task and grader, and the structured arm is far smaller than the comparator ('Token counts are between 8k and 12k' vs '53k to 61k'), which meets the not-larger criterion. The evidence is weak, though: means differ by about 0.1 and 'average scores alone are insufficient for declaring a method as a definitive winner'.
graph_class_check: n/a (repo_map_skeleton/hybrid; no call graph, AST or CPG)

comparison: Table 1: Raw (zero-shot) vs Raw+ICL (one-shot with DSL grammar summary + one demonstration) vs FT (QLoRA). Cleanest: Raw vs Raw+ICL.
model_config: Same base model per pair (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B or DeepSeek-Coder-7B). FT changes weights.
dataset_metric: 105 held-out BMW Xtext-DSL tasks; Exact Match, Valid JSON, BLEU, Change Similarity, Structural correctness
budget_control: Not controlled or reported. All arms get the full linearized-JSON project context ('without truncation'), and ICL adds a grammar summary and a demonstration.
arm_a: Raw+ICL: instruction + full linearized JSON project + DSL grammar summary + one demonstration
arm_b: Raw: instruction + full linearized JSON project
other_changes: Raw vs ICL: none apart from the added prompt material. FT arm: fine-tuning (multi-change).
rationale: Same model and single-call setup, but ICL adds prompt content with no budget held ('In one-shot setting, we add a compact summary of DSL grammar rules and a single instruction–output demonstration'). The repository representation itself (linearized JSON) is never compared with an alternative representation; minimal-context variants appear only in training.

comparison: Table 3 downstream restricted-context validation: explorer outputs (K=5 regions) fed to a fixed patcher. Cleanest same-interface pair: TF-IDF vs BM25 vs RAG (Potion) chunk retrievers. Upstream nDCG@500 is a retrieval metric with no generating model.
model_config: Fixed patcher: Mini-SWE-Agent with GPT-5.4 (Table 3; §4.2 averages GPT-5.4 and Gemini-3-Pro), with 'same patcher, prompt template, tool set, and interaction budget'. Explorers themselves differ in scaffold and LLM.
dataset_metric: SWE-Explore n=150 subset; SWE-bench harness resolve rate (upstream: HitFile, Recall, nDCG@500, etc.)
budget_control: Nominal count only: each explorer returns 'at most K=5' regions, but region length is unconstrained ('CoSIL again emits whole files'; others 'under-fill the top-5 budget, emitting only one region'). B=500 lines applies only to scoring nDCG@500/Rec@B, not to the context given to the patcher. Realized lines per arm are not reported.
arm_a: TF-IDF top-5 chunks (issue text as query)
arm_b: BM25 top-5 chunks (or Potion dense top-5), same chunk-and-rank interface
other_changes: Lexical/dense pair: none reported. Agentic and graph localizers (LocAgent, CoSIL, OrcaLoca) vs general agents and retrievers differ in scaffold, LLM and number of calls.
delta: Resolve rate TF-IDF 26.0% vs BM25 12.7% vs RAG 23.3%; CoSIL 59.3%, Mini-SWE-Agent 50.0%, Oracle 59.7%, Random 4.7%
rationale: The patcher is fixed and only the selected context differs, but realized context size is not equalized; only the region count is: 'an ordered list of at most K=5 repository-relative line regions'. The B=500 line budget governs metric scoring, not model input. The record's 'budget_matched_ablation' label is not supported.
graph_class_check: call_dep_graph is listed but is not primary (hybrid). No budget-matched comparison exists for the graph-based localizers (LocAgent, CoSIL): they differ in scaffold, and CoSIL's output size (whole files) is uncontrolled.

comparison: §3.2 / Figure 3: single-turn diff-only vs single-turn diff+context (same reviewer). Agentic review vs single-turn is the headline.
model_config: Reviewer fixed to Claude Opus 4.6 in all three settings. PRs from GLM-5, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B and Qwen3-30B-A3B.
dataset_metric: SWE-Review-Bench (1,384 PRs); decision accuracy (DA) and resolve rate after revision (RRR)
budget_control: Not controlled. Diff+context adds affected pre-change source files ('For files exceeding 500 lines, only 100 lines of context around each diff hunk are included'). The agentic arm uses about 148K tokens on average; single-turn token counts are not reported.
other_changes: Diff-only vs diff+context: none. Agentic vs single-turn: multi-turn tool loop with many more calls (multi-change).
delta: Not given numerically in the text: 'adding retrieved context generally improves over diff-only review' (values only in Figure 3). Agentic vs best single-turn RRR (Qwen3-30B-A3B PRs): 52.6% vs 44.1%.
rationale: Same model and a single call; only the provided context differs, and it differs in amount with no budget held. The authors' 'not merely having more context' claim rests on the agentic arm, which also changes the scaffold.

comparison: Table 1: SWE-Pruner Pro vs No Pruning and vs six prior pruners (LLMLingua2, Selective Context, RAG, Self-Prune, LongCodeZip, SWE-Pruner) with matched agent configuration. Cleanest: SWE-Pruner Pro vs SWE-Pruner / No Pruning.
model_config: Same backbone per block (Qwen3-Coder-Next or MiMo-V2-Flash): 'All pruners on the same backbone share identical decoding, harness, and hardware'. Max 250 turns. GPT-5.4-mini judge.
dataset_metric: SWE-QA, SWE-QA-Pro (LLM-judge score 1-10), Oolong (accuracy); total prompt+completion tokens
budget_control: Not capped; realized total tokens are reported per arm, and the proposed arm uses the fewest tokens in every cell (e.g., Qwen3-Coder-Next SWE-QA-Pro: 368K vs 433K SWE-Pruner vs 607K No Pruning)
arm_a: SWE-Pruner Pro: tool outputs pruned line-by-line by a trained head on the frozen backbone's hidden states
arm_b: SWE-Pruner (separate scoring model with a goal-hint query), or No Pruning (raw tool outputs)
other_changes: Agent turns and API calls vary endogenously (e.g., SWE-bench Qwen calls 131.9 -> 139.8). Comparator pruners carry their own components (separate scorer, extra Self-Prune call). Pro's head is trained, but the backbone is frozen.
delta: Qwen3-Coder-Next SWE-QA-Pro: 7.84 vs 7.36 (SWE-Pruner) vs 7.60 (No Pruning), at 368K vs 433K vs 607K tokens (-39.4% vs no pruning)
rationale: Only the pruning module is swapped ('swapping only the pruning module'), and the proposed arm's realized token use is not larger than any comparator's ('SWE-Pruner Pro again achieves the lowest token count on every cell'). Caveat: budget is an outcome rather than a held constant, and the multi-turn trajectories differ endogenously.

comparison: Table 3 ablation (DyCoder vs w/o Similarity-based, w/o DyRetriever, w/o Multi-hop Reasoning). Also Table 1/2 vs Direct, SimpleRAG, RLCoder, AlignCoder and RepoScope (static graph).
dataset_metric: CoderEval and DevEval; Pass@1 and #Token (all LLM interaction tokens)
budget_control: Not controlled; realized tokens reported and very unequal. CoderEval Qwen3: DyCoder 13.09k, w/o DyRetriever 4.67k, w/o Multi-hop 6.81k, w/o Similarity 11.61k; RepoScope 5.11k.
arm_a: DyCoder: similarity context plus DyRetriever (LLM-guided multi-hop select/visit/expand over a dynamically built partial dependency graph)
other_changes: DyRetriever adds multiple LLM reasoning calls (up to 10 hops), so the number of model calls and the pipeline stages differ. The baselines are different systems, some trained (RLCoder, AlignCoder).
delta: CoderEval Qwen3-Coder-30B Pass@1 49.48 vs 41.57 (-16.0%) at 13.09k vs 4.67k tokens; w/o Multi-hop 46.52 at 6.81k
rationale: Every ablation removes or adds LLM-driven retrieval stages, which changes the number of model calls as well as context, and the graph arm uses 1.95-2.43x more tokens ('DyCoder consumes 1.95-2.43 times more tokens').
graph_class_check: Primary class is call_dep_graph. No budget-matched comparison exists: the graph-based arms always use more tokens and extra LLM calls than the comparators, including static-graph RepoScope (5.11k vs 13.09k).
